I'll briefly explain the design of the refactoring.

Done. The spec (.docs/instructions.md) is a refactoring exercise: the original code worked but was confusing, and the goal is to rewrite it for readability while keeping all tests passing. I did exactly that — only `markdown.go` was changed; `markdown_test.go` and `cases_test.go` are untouched, and no new files were created. ## What the refactor does The old implementation was a single character-by-character loop juggling five pieces of ad-hoc state (`header`, `pos`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`), with subtle quirks like re-interpreting a `#` in the middle of a line as a header marker and using `strings.LastIndex` checks on the whole document to decide when to close a list. The rewrite in `markdown.go` is a line-based parser, which matches how markdown is actually structured: 1. **`applyEmphasis`** — resolves the first `__bold__` / `_italic__` pair on the whole document, exactly the four single replacements the original did (order preserved: strong before em). 2. **`Render`** — splits the input into lines and classifies each one in a single `switch`: header, list item, or paragraph. The only state left is one `inList` flag, and `closeList` closes the `
    ` whenever a non-list line (or end of input) follows a list — which is what makes the "list closes properly with preceding and following lines" test pass. 3. **`headerLevel` / `renderHeader`** — a header is a line starting with 1–6 `#`s followed by a space; 7+ `#`s fall through to a paragraph. The rest of the line is kept verbatim, so `#` and `*` inside header text are never re-interpreted (simpler than the old code's `he`/`header--` dance, same output). 4. **`isListItem` / `renderListItem`** — a `* `-prefixed line becomes `
  • text
    • `, text kept verbatim. As the spec suggests, the refactoring notes are captured in comments on `Render` and the helpers. ## Verification - `go test -v ./...` — all 16 test cases in `TestMarkdown` pass (baseline before the rewrite also passed, so behavior is preserved). - `gofmt -l` and `go vet` — both clean.
